Timeline::from_ymdhms¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

static Timeline Timeline::from_ymdhms(
    const Series& year,
    const Series& month,
    const Series& day,
    const Series& hour,
    const Series& minute,
    const Series& second,
    std::string_view tz_name = "UTC")

Assemble Local Date And Clock Fields¶

from_ymdhms() extends from_ymd() with whole-second clock components. It forms each local civil timestamp in tz_name, resolves that timestamp to UTC storage, and preserves the shared component shape.

const auto year = pluss::make_series(2024LL);
const auto month = pluss::make_series({2LL, 3LL});
const auto day = pluss::make_series({29LL, 1LL});
const auto hour = pluss::make_series({6LL, 7LL});
const auto minute = pluss::make_series(30LL);
const auto second = pluss::make_series(45LL);

const auto times = pluss::Timeline::from_ymdhms(
    year, month, day, hour, minute, second, "UTC");
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(times) << '\n';

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[2], tz=UTC)
[ 2024-02-29 06:30:45, 2024-03-01 07:30:45 ]

Here year, minute, and second are scalars and broadcast; the other components establish shape [2]. Valid clock ranges are hour 0..23, minute 0..59, and second 0..59. Invalid fields throw. If any component at a position is Timeline::kNaT, that position becomes NaT.

The constructor has whole-second precision. Begin with epoch nanoseconds when subsecond fields must be represented exactly.

Timezone Boundaries¶

Components describe local wall time, not UTC fields wearing a timezone label. Offset rules therefore affect the stored epoch tick. Ambiguous and nonexistent local clocks are resolved by the constructor’s timezone policy; avoid such wall times when an explicit fold or gap policy is required.
